gaps.sentence: 'I'm looking for a flat near the hospital,' she explained. She explained that she ___ for a flat near the hospital.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous in reported speech: was looking.

gaps.sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
gaps.explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
They ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed them.
gaps.explanation: Deny + -ing reports a rejection of the accusation; 'but nobody believed them' confirms the meaning.

gaps.sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
gaps.explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.
